source: SkillsInjector (arXiv 2605.29794) — Yanchao Li et al., Nanjing University / Shanghai AI Lab
summary: Dynamic skill context construction for LLM agents: a two-stage system that selects which skills to admit per task (context planner) and adapts descriptions based on co-injected skills (set-aware renderer). Reports +3.9–7.3pp gains over baselines on tau2-bench, SkillsBench, ALFWorld.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to the confirmed gap that executor prompts don't receive distilled skills (plannerAgent.ts injects skills via options.priorSkills; executorAgent.ts has no equivalent). Selective injection pattern is well-motivated and feasible within existing agentSkillRepository architecture.

source: Prime Intellect Prime Agent — self-improving coding harness (August 2026)
summary: MIT-licensed self-improving coding agent using a persistent IPython kernel and Recursive Language Model (RLM) pattern. A /refine command reviews execution history and makes targeted updates to working state without rewriting the system prompt. Reports 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 (vs 95.4% human expert baseline — company-reported).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the self-refinement loop is interesting but maps to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory), which already tracks the run-outcome memory gap. The IPython kernel approach is incompatible with AgentForge's CLI-subprocess architecture.

summary: LangGraph 1.1.x adds type-safe streaming via opt-in version='v2' format, GraphOutput objects with .value and .interrupts, DeltaChannel checkpoints, distributed runtime, and CLI deploy commands. v1.1.1–1.1.6 fix replay behavior for subgraphs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — LangGraph is a Python graph-based orchestration framework; AgentForge uses a TypeScript deterministic state machine. Streaming and checkpointing features are architecturally different from AgentForge's SSE + Prisma artifact model.

summary: Microsoft shipped Agent Framework 1.0 (April 3 2026) merging AutoGen + Semantic Kernel with enterprise checkpointing, pause/resume, and human-in-the-loop. CrewAI under active development with A2A task utilities and Flows human-in-the-loop support.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — these are Python orchestration frameworks; AgentForge's TypeScript/Fastify architecture and CLI-subprocess model are fundamentally different. AgentForge already has its own state machine and human approval steps.

source: AI agent memory architecture overview — Analytics Vidhya / klu.ai / HackerNoon (2026)
summary: 2026 consensus on four-tier agent memory taxonomy: episodic (autobiographical event logs), semantic (distilled facts/preferences via vector DB), procedural (skills/rules), working (context window). Consolidation step periodically converts episodic to semantic. Tooling: Mem0, Letta, Zep.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic/semantic split is relevant but AgentForge already ships skill distillation (procedural memory) and HID-188 tracks episodic run-outcome memory injection. Semantic consolidation (distillation) already present in distillationAgent.ts.

source: Karpathy 'Agentic Engineering' — The Decoder / Anthropic move (2026)
summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' (February 2026) and reversed his October 2025 skepticism about agent reliability. He joined Anthropic's pre-training team. Key insight: agents still need high-level direction, judgment, taste, and oversight from humans.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — directional commentary on the field, no specific implementable pattern for AgentForge.
